summary: E. W. Adikaram worked in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of London, where he studied under William Stede (attested 1946).

Eberhard Sandschneider, a scholar in Sinology and other fields, studied at Saarland University (~1974–1981). He held posts at Mainz (1995–1998), the Free University of Berlin (1998), and the German Council on Foreign Relations (2003–2016).

Edeltraud Harzer works in Indology and philosophy. She studied at Charles University, the University of Washington, and under Shree Narayan Mishra and Ram Shankar Bhattacharya. She held posts at Puget Sound, Washington, Stanford, Indiana, and Texas at Austin (1998).
Edith Wyschogrod worked in philosophy and religious studies. She studied at Hunter College and Columbia University, and served on the faculty at Rice University from approximately 1992 to 2003.
Edmond Yee works in religious studies and Sinology. Around 1984, he held faculty posts at the Pacific Lutheran Theological Seminary and the Graduate Theological Union.

Edmund Hardy worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg and Berlin, and served as Professor of Philosophy at Freiburg (1885–1893) and professor at Fribourg (~1893–1898).

Edmund Leach worked in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Clare College, King's College, and the LSE, studying under Bronislaw Malinowski (~1937–1939). He held a post at Cambridge (~1953–1978).
Edmund Nathaniel Snyder was an Indologist. He graduated as valedictorian from Harvard University by 1886 and studied under Albrecht Weber and Hermann Oldenberg.

Edo Shonin works in religious and Buddhist studies. In 2015, he was attested as a research psychologist at Nottingham Trent University and Research Director at the Awake to Wisdom Centre for Meditation and Mindfulness Research.

Eduard Hermann was a linguist and Indologist who studied under Berthold Delbrück (~1891–1895). He held posts at the University of Kiel (~1913–1917), Goethe University Frankfurt (~1917–1924), and the University of Göttingen (~1924–1940).
Eduard Müller was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He studied at Leipzig University (~1871–1874) and served as a professor at the University of Bern (~1887–1908).

Eduard Sachau worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Kiel and Leipzig (under Hermann Brockhaus), and held posts at Vienna, Humboldt/Frederick William University Berlin, and the Seminar for Oriental Languages.

Eduard Sievers was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University and Frederick William University Berlin. He held professorial posts at Jena (1871–1883), Tübingen (1883–1887), Halle-Wittenberg (1887–1892), and Leipzig (1892–1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach works in Buddhist studies. He earned a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014), where he was supervised by Y. Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.
Edward Albert Gait was a scholar in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at University College London (~1880–1882) and founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian/Central Asian studies. He studied at Charterhouse School and Merton College, later serving as Professor of Hindústání at East India Company College (~1845–1857) and at the Foreign Office.

Edward Byles Cowell worked in Indology and Buddhist studies. Educated at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson, he served as Principal of Sanskrit College, Professor of History at Presidency University, and Professor at Cambridge (1867, 1887).
Edward C. Dimock worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Yale University (~1949–1953) and held a post at the University of Chicago from approximately 1957 to 1992.
Edward Clive Bayley was a scholar in Indology, history, and archaeology. He studied at the East India Company College and Haileybury (~1840–1842), entering the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze worked in Buddhist studies and Indology. After studying at Bonn and Cologne, he held posts at London, the University of Washington, UC Berkeley, Lancaster University, and served as Vice-President of the Buddhist Society.
